evidence: Q2 2026 da Vinci procedures grew approximately 15% and Ion procedures approximately 36% while installed bases expanded 12% and 21%, respectively.
Da Vinci 5 represented 246 of 468 Q2 placements, indicating an active platform transition rather than dependence on a mature installed base alone.
counter_evidence: U.S. da Vinci procedure growth was approximately 12%, below OUS growth, and bariatric procedures declined high-single digits.
Multiple credible competitors now have U.S. regulatory authorization or active indication expansion, reducing the certainty of category leadership persistence.

evidence: Approximately 76.3% of Q2 revenue came from instruments/accessories and service, consistent with procedure-linked recurring-like economics around a large installed base.
Ion procedures grew 36% despite only 2% placement growth in Q2, supporting utilization-driven customer value after installation.
counter_evidence: Hospitals face capital-budget pressure and more than half of Q2 da Vinci placements were leases, implying customers increasingly value flexible financing rather than outright system purchases.
Recent FDA field actions create a product-quality monitoring burden even though current procedure growth remains strong.

evidence: The installed-base, training, clinical workflow, instrument consumption and service flywheel continues to expand, with 11,710 da Vinci systems installed at Q2 end.
Da Vinci 5 and Ion provide additional technology and procedure expansion vectors inside the existing ecosystem.
counter_evidence: Johnson & Johnson OTTAVA obtained U.S. De Novo authorization in July 2026, Medtronic Hugo is cleared in U.S. urology with additional indications submitted, and CMR Versius is FDA-cleared.
A Class I SureForm recall plus multiple Class II da Vinci 5/SP field actions raise the evidence threshold for assuming the moat will widen without interruption.

evidence: TTM OCF was approximately $3.7064B and mechanical OCF-minus-PPE FCF approximately $3.2224B; H1 OCF increased strongly while PPE purchases declined year over year.
Basic and diluted weighted-average share counts declined year over year, so current growth is not being financed through persistent net dilution.
counter_evidence: 254 of 468 Q2 da Vinci placements were operating leases and working-capital changes used approximately $870M of H1 cash, including substantial inventory growth, increasing capital carried by Intuitive.
A conservative FCF-minus-income-statement-SBC diagnostic is only about $2.3831B, showing that headline mechanical FCF overstates owner cash if compensation is treated economically.

evidence: The company maintains heavy R&D and platform reinvestment, transitioned selected European distributor territories to direct distribution for approximately $533M, and preserves a very strong balance sheet.
Executive compensation includes performance-based equity and the CEO/Executive Chair transition is disclosed with board oversight.
counter_evidence: H1 2026 repurchases averaged $475.67 per share, materially above the September 9 reference price of $353.24; this does not prove intrinsic-value destruction but requires stricter repurchase-price discipline review.
Executive/director beneficial ownership is modest at roughly 0.6% as a group.

evidence: Cash, cash equivalents and investments were approximately $8.63B at June 30, 2026 versus total liabilities of about $2.58B, with no material borrowing dependence identified.
TTM operating cash flow exceeds $3.7B and the company can self-fund R&D, leasing and repurchases without structural reliance on external financing.
counter_evidence: Leasing and inventory intensity can absorb more cash as the installed base grows, but current liquidity is sufficient to absorb this without threatening solvency.

evidence: At the September 9 reference price of $353.24, the retained base scenario is about $302.71 per share and the reverse model requires approximately 12.56% annual growth in years 2-10 at a 9% hurdle.
Current procedure growth around the mid-teens means the reverse requirement is demanding but not obviously equivalent to an unrealistic bull case.

structural_thesis: Intuitive remains the dominant procedure-linked robotic-surgery ecosystem with a growing installed base and recurring instrument/service economics. Da Vinci 5 and Ion extend the runway, but the U.S. competitive landscape has materially changed and the moat must now be demonstrated against credible alternatives rather than inferred from a historically sparse field.
economic_finding: The business converts procedure growth into strong operating cash flow, but rising operating-lease intensity places more systems and inventory on Intuitive's balance sheet. The correct long-term test is FCF per share after SBC and required lease/inventory reinvestment, not procedure growth alone.
capital_and_survival: Survivability is exceptional. Capital-allocation quality is less perfect: H1 repurchases averaged materially above the current reference price, while the European direct-distribution acquisition should be judged on incremental cash returns rather than strategic narrative alone.
macro_overlay: The stored higher-for-longer macro regime increases hospital-capex and valuation discount-rate stress but does not change the company-quality score. ISRG's balance sheet limits refinancing risk.
falsifiers: Da Vinci procedure growth remains below 10% for four consecutive quarters while competitor placements, procedures or hospital switching materially increase.
Procedure volume remains positive but instruments/accessories economics or gross margin structurally decline because of pricing concessions or competition.
Da Vinci 5, SP, Ion or instrument recalls broaden into material patient-harm evidence, procedure pauses or regulatory restrictions.
Lease intensity, inventory and PP&E growth cause FCF per share to persistently lag procedure growth after SBC and required reinvestment.
Hospital capital/funding constraints materially reduce placements and utilization fails to compensate.
increase_evidence: Da Vinci 5 international rollout and new functionality increase utilization and procedure economics without margin deterioration.
Competitor entry expands the robotic-surgery category without material loss of Intuitive procedure share, placements or pricing power.
FCF per share grows at a durable low-to-mid-teens rate with SBC controlled and diluted share count flat or declining.
FDA field actions close without evidence of a broader systemic quality problem.
Price falls below a conservative/base intrinsic-value range or verified owner cash rises enough to create a clear margin of safety at the 9% hurdle.
next_evidence: Quarterly da Vinci 5 utilization and OUS placement mix, including feedback-enabled procedure adoption.
OTTAVA/Hugo/Versius U.S. placements, procedure volumes and hospital multi-platform adoption.
Recall closure status, MDR/adverse-event trends and any regulatory restrictions.
Eight-quarter bridge for leased systems, inventory, PP&E, procedure growth and owner FCF per share.
Incremental economics of the 2026 European direct-distribution acquisition.
Repurchase price discipline relative to contemporaneous intrinsic value.

attacks: The moat may look strongest immediately before broad U.S. competition becomes commercially relevant.
Procedure growth can hide economic deterioration if leasing and incentives rise faster than recurring cash economics.
The 76% recurring-like revenue mix is not contractual recurring revenue; it depends on actual surgical utilization.
Large installed-base switching costs can protect share but may not prevent price compression in new placements.
Class I/II recalls may remain isolated, but a high-valuation medical-device company has asymmetric downside to a systemic safety event.
Da Vinci 5 replacement demand can temporarily lift placements without permanently increasing procedure TAM.
Ion growth may require a distinct commercial and capital model and should not automatically inherit da Vinci economics.
Repurchases above subsequent market prices may indicate less disciplined valuation judgment than the operating record suggests.
Hospital reimbursement, staffing and capital budgets can slow robotic adoption independently of patient demand.
A 12.56% long-duration reverse growth requirement leaves limited room for a decade of normalization if competition compresses mature owner margins.

final_conclusion: ISRG remains a high-quality Emerging Outlier but is not buy-authorized. The operating franchise is stronger than the valuation asymmetry, and two open vetoes—moat shrinkage and permanent-loss probability—must remain INVESTIGATE because credible U.S. competition and recent product-quality actions are now real. WATCH/P1 is appropriate until either evidence closes those risks or valuation creates a materially wider margin of safety.
